title: kāyagatā sati sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en:
At Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned
and the path leading to the unconditioned. Listen to that.

And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned?
The destruction of craving, the destruction of aversion,
the destruction of delusion:
this is called the unconditioned.

And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned? Awareness directed to the body:
this is called the path leading to the unconditioned.

Thus, bhikkhus, I have taught you the unconditioned
and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Whatever should be done, bhikkhus, by a compassionate teacher out of compassion for his disciples,
desiring their welfare, that I have done for you.

These are the feet of trees, bhikkhus, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent,
lest you regret it later.
This is our instruction to you.”

“… Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will develop and cultivate awareness directed
to the body, make it our vehicle, make it our basis,
stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully undertake it.’ Thus should you train yourselves.”
